title: JavaScript Objects Core Check
description: Check your understanding of object literals, properties, methods, dynamic keys, and object inspection methods.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: Which syntax creates a JavaScript object literal?
questions.explanation: Object literals use curly braces and key-value pairs, such as `{ name: "Alice" }`.
Dot notation accesses the value of the `title` property.

questions.prompt: When should bracket notation be used?

options.text: When the property name is stored in a variable or is not a valid identifier
Only when the object is empty

questions.explanation: Bracket notation is useful for dynamic property names and names like `"dark-mode"` or `"font size"`.
`user.key` looks for a property literally named `key`. To use the variable, write `user[key]`.

options.text: A function stored as a property on an object
Any property whose value is a string
A variable declared inside an array

questions.explanation: A method is a function that belongs to an object as one of its properties.

questions.prompt: Which object uses method shorthand correctly?
questions.explanation: Method shorthand uses `methodName(parameters) { ... }` inside an object literal.
Computed property names evaluate the expression inside `[]`, so `[key]` becomes `email`.
`Object.keys()` returns an array of property names.
`Object.values()` returns an array of property values.
`Object.entries()` returns an array of `[key, value]` pairs.

questions.prompt: How can you count the number of normal own properties in an object?
questions.explanation: Objects do not have array-style `.length`; `Object.keys(object).length` counts the keys returned in an array.

questions.prompt: What is the best structure for a list of users where each user has an id and name?
questions.explanation: An array of objects is the standard shape when you have an ordered list of records with named fields.
